why: The notes are cut off right where they reach the idiom. Calvin's note stops at 'visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon…', Keil and Delitzsch stop at 'He does not leave sin…', and Matthew Henry only covers 'will by no means clear the guilty'. None of them explains what visiting the fathers' iniquity on the children means. The idiom list's meaning (disease, poverty, bad example, idolatry) is not supported by the notes, so I can't write a meaning without adding outside information.
